evidence: All gating files parse on the frozen bytes. Python tomllib parses task.toml (schema_version, artifacts, task, metadata, agent, environment, verifier), tests/scoring.toml (gates/weights/floors) and all five judge.toml files without error. Beyond plain TOML, rewardkit 0.1.7's own loader (rewardkit.runner.discover) in the pinned verifier image cw-editor-verifier:current, with tests mounted read-only and no judge call, built every dimension: gates constraints and render (AgentJudge, batched, 600s, 1 criterion each), scored functional (AgentJudge, individual, 550s, 16 criteria), polish (batched, 900s, 6) and visual (batched, 900s, 4). The models.py JudgeMode Literal['batched','individual'] confirms the non-template functional mode='individual' is a supported value. bash -n passes for tests/test.sh, solution/solve.sh and the app-restart.sh heredoc that test.sh generates (I extracted and checked it separately). Both have #!/bin/bash shebangs, `file` reports plain ASCII, and a grep for  over the whole task tree and a UTF-8 BOM scan found nothing. test.sh, solve.sh, both Dockerfiles, score.py, restart_mcp.py and scoring.toml are byte-identical to the frozen template. task.toml differs only in metadata and the task identity fields. score.py and restart_mcp.py pass ast.parse. Both seed_data.json files and package.json parse as JSON (seed hashes match each other, b256f85e...). Reference entry: node --check passes for solution/app/server.js and public/app.js. server.js reads PORT and DB_PATH (lines 13-14) and listens on 0.0.0.0 (line 528), which matches test.sh's launch. Every prompt.md contains exactly one {app_context} and one {criteria}. Would-run evidence: the raw-evidence-index entries re-hash True, and their matching_source_files hashes equal the current frozen solution bytes. The scripted golden run (qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/results/golden-run.log) shows the app installed by the frozen solve.sh starting ('Kittle & Rowe matter chat on port 3000' twice, around a real restart, pids 28->57) and all scripted checks PASS. Plausible broken app: a submission with no /app/server.js, a symlink escape or a non-listening server makes test.sh exit 0 with the pre-written zero reward (write_zero_reward then the ensure_reward trap), so a broken submission cannot crash grading. A conforming alternative app is unaffected by this row, because the entry contract is server.js on port 3000, set by the public brief and the template. Scope limit: this is parser, loader and scripted-golden evidence. No full configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists for these exact bytes (the index says so). The hosted v2 runs used previous bytes, though they also exercised mode='individual'. That gap belongs to the runtime, workload and reward rows. It is not a parse defect for this row. Reviewer hygiene: py_compile briefly created tests/tools/__pycache__/score.cpython-312.pyc in the frozen cache. I deleted it immediately and confirmed no __pycache__ or .pyc remains. The Docker probes used --rm with no new images, and no qc51 containers are left.
